graveyard.value: cupel-residue
graveyard.epitaph: Three canvas layers is two too many. The cupel-residue particles were indistinguishable from the cupellation canvas at normal viewing. Consolidating to two canvases: touchstone-surface (interactive) and cupellation-canvas (ambient). Less is more when everything is subtle.

graveyard.value: gen10-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen12-css. The liminal-era palette and dawn-furnace timing rules are replaced by the crucible palette.

graveyard.value: 76°F, 74% humidity at dawn in South Florida. The air is already warm enough to patinate copper. Nothing here gets to stay bright.
graveyard.epitaph: Weakest night thought — too abstract, drifting into aphorism territory without enough concrete image.

graveyard.value: Cupellation: you heat the impure metal in a bone-ash cup and blow air across it.
graveyard.epitaph: Redundant with the new night thought about touchstones. Two touchstone metaphors in one pool is one too many.

graveyard.name: metallurgy
graveyard.epitaph: The metallurgy epoch proved the evolutionary system works. 11 generations, 20 kills, a touchstone simulator, canvas animations, five interaction patterns invented and three killed. It did its job: it proved the organism can evolve. Now it sheds its skin entirely.

graveyard.value: gen1-css
graveyard.epitaph: Twelve generations old. Whatever styles this carried have been superseded six times over. Archaeological dignity demands burial.

graveyard.value: swarm-memory
graveyard.epitaph: The swarm-memory DOM layer was invisible in the screenshot — ghost dots that never materialized into anything perceptible. The new murmuration-trails canvas replaces its function with actual visual presence.

graveyard.value: touchstone-streak:-when-user-c
graveyard.epitaph: Carried over from the metallurgy epoch. The touchstone-surface canvas no longer exists in this epoch — the interaction description references dead infrastructure. The swarm-scatter click interaction is the new primary interaction.

graveyard.value: murmuration-trails
graveyard.epitaph: Invisible in the screenshot. A canvas layer drawing faint arc segments that no one could see against the particle field. The idea was good — afterimages of swarm motion — but the implementation was too subtle to register. If the concept returns, it should be in the WebGL layer, not a separate DOM canvas.

graveyard.value: debasement-hover:-when-user-ho
graveyard.epitaph: A metallurgy-epoch relic. Text flickering between real and debased versions — clever when the obsession was assaying and counterfeit detection, meaningless in the swarm epoch. The trust-erosion concept was interesting but never visible enough to register. If trust becomes a theme again, rebuild it from scratch.

graveyard.value: gen14-css
graveyard.epitaph: One generation old. Superseded by the gen15 overhaul — new overlay structure, new color palette, new section architecture.

graveyard.value: gen15-css

graveyard.value: 76°F, 74% humidity. Copper would be greening right now. There's a Portuguese word — azinhavre — for the verdigris that forms on copper exposed to air. It's the metal's diary. Corrosion as autobiography.
graveyard.epitaph: Too generic. 'The screen becomes a surface for projection' — vague, no image. Replaced with weather-specific and gold-specific thoughts that anchor to today.

graveyard.value: depth-motes
graveyard.epitaph: Invisible in the screenshot. 40 DOM-based motes at 12% opacity producing no visible effect. The pulse-rings section replaces this with a visible, rhythmic element. Better to have one noticeable thing than two invisible things.

graveyard.value: gen16-css
graveyard.epitaph: Pulse rings were invisible in the screenshot. The threshold-veil radial gradient and flock-canvas replace the visual strategy entirely.

graveyard.value: A murmuration is a shape that no bird intended. The best pages work the same way — you set the rules, the form surprises you.
graveyard.epitaph: Weakest morning thought. Generic observation about swarm behavior without a concrete image.

graveyard.value: The touchstone tested purity by leaving a streak. The swarm tests purity by leaving a pattern. Both require a dark surface.
graveyard.epitaph: Stale night thought from the metallurgy-to-swarm transition. No longer relevant to the threshold mood.

graveyard.epitaph: Old metallurgy-era secret about cupellation that no longer connects to anything on the page.

graveyard.value: flock-canvas
graveyard.epitaph: The two-layer flock experiment failed. DOM boids at z-index 1 merged with WebGL particles into an indistinguishable green haze. The effect was invisible in the screenshot — just more murk. Kill it, reduce layers, let the WebGL field breathe alone.

graveyard.value: pulse-rings
graveyard.epitaph: Three concentric CSS circles expanding and fading. Invisible in the screenshot for two generations running. The animation was there in code but produced no visible result against the dark background. Dead weight.

graveyard.value: stream-fades
graveyard.epitaph: Gradient overlays meant to dissolve the stream edges. In practice they just added more darkness to an already-too-dark page. The stream itself needs rethinking, not softening.

graveyard.value: thought-stream
graveyard.epitaph: The consciousness stream section dominated the viewport in every screenshot — a wall of monospaced text that made the site look like a blog. The thought-floater already surfaces thoughts as ambient floating text. The stream was redundant and visually overwhelming. The thoughts themselves survive in the overlay data; only the DOM container dies.

graveyard.value: gen17-css
graveyard.epitaph: Superseded by gen18 CSS. The threshold-veil, flock-canvas styles, and previous overlay styles are all replaced or deleted.

graveyard.value: Halfway through anything is the worst place to assess it.
graveyard.epitaph: Weakest afternoon thought — generic swarm observation without specificity.

graveyard.value: ambient-data
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced by the compass element in overlay-bottom. Redundant.

graveyard.value: gen18-css

graveyard.value: Craig Reynolds published 'Flocks, Herds and Schools' in 1987. Three rules. Forty years later we still can't improve on them. Some problems were solved on the first attempt.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with Craig Reynolds thought — more specific, more useful.

graveyard.value: There's a Portuguese word for the moment a flock turns as one: revoada. It also means uprising.
graveyard.epitaph: Replaced with revoada thought — the Portuguese-swarm connection is stronger than the previous generic evening observation.
